title: Licence To Kill
build: G64 disk image of a Trilogic Expert freezer backup, loaded by a fast loader (BOND) and frozen in the first second after the game started; the listing comes from memory resumed at the program's first instruction, $07F8. A second disk holds another build of the same program, 16 bytes longer

tools.subagents: one checker agent for the 60-comment sample; one reader agent for the review; one agent for everything else
tools.widget tests: node 22: the music player runs against the game's code on the kit's 6502 simulator (test_music.js)

exclude: zero page the game does not use: BASIC's and the KERNAL's. $22 appears only as the snapshot's value of the pointer operand at $0A81, which copy_tile_row sets before each use
the KERNAL's work area and vectors: the game writes only the screen page $0288 and the interrupt vector $0314/$0315, which are the system's
the rest of the cassette buffer, which nothing reads
the KERNAL's text screen, which draw_picture_tiles uses as the work area for the pictures that slide onto the play screen; the image holds what was there when the backup was made
runtime: the two play screens at $4000 and $4400 and their sprite pointers, redrawn by the game
runtime: the character set in use, copied here by copy_charset from $D000, $D600, $DC00, $E200 or $E800 at each level and at the title
runtime: characters the game draws into, the shots at $4E00 and the panel's gauges from $4E80 (init_panel_chars, draw_bar_gauge_1, draw_gauge_2_top and _bottom)
include: the character sets for levels 1 to 3 at $D000, $D600 and $DC00, under the I/O area; copy_charset reads them with the I/O banked out

io: copy_charset banks the I/O out from $205A to $208C
